text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. speaker: Doctor

Thank you for that information. Does the rash extend to other areas of the body, such as the diaper area or behind the ears?

Also, has the baby been fed any new foods or introduced to any new skincare products recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The presence of greasy yellow scales on the scalp and forehead in a 3-month-old infant is highly characteristic of infantile seborrheic dermatitis, commonly known as cradle cap. I will proceed with the diagnosis based on this classic clinical presentation.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Infantile Seborrheic Dermatitis
